interest: Shows ordinary Americans, from a Dallas travel agent to a thirteen-year-old student, writing to the State Department about Japan.
overview: This decimal file (894.00, Political Affairs of Japan) covering late October through late December 1944 consists of miscellaneous State Department records, including cross-reference sheets and public correspondence concerning wartime Japan. It contains a cross-reference sheet for a Soviet lecture by K. T. Eidus on "Japan at War," public correspondence with a Dallas travel agent offering pre-war Japanese promotional tourist literature for government use, an exchange between a thirteen-year-old Arkansas boy and the Division of Japanese Affairs regarding Joseph C. Grew's appointment and recommended readings on Japanese history, and a confidential cross-reference sheet reporting the evacuation of the Portuguese diplomatic corps from Tokyo. Together, these disparate documents illustrate the diverse inquiries, citizen contributions, and intelligence indexing processed by the Division of Japanese Affairs during the late stages of World War II.

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting a telegram from the USSR concerning a lecture delivered by K. T. Eidus on 'Japan at War'.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram No. 4104 (October 26, 1944) on K. T. Eidus's Soviet lecture 'Japan at War.'
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Lecture by K. T. Eidus on 'Japan at War'

subfiles.about: A Dallas travel agent submits pre-war Japanese tourist brochures to the Secretary of State for potential government use during the war.
subfiles.summary: Dallas travel agent Fred L. Haskett sends Secretary Stettinius two Japanese tourist folders from 1938–39, asking for their return if not needed.
subfiles.title: Letter from Fred L. Haskett to Edward R. Stettinius Jr. Transmitting Japanese Tourist Literature

subfiles.about: The Chief of the Division of Japanese Affairs thanks a Dallas travel agent for offering Japanese tourist circulars and returns them.
subfiles.summary: Erle R. Dickover thanks Fred L. Haskett for the Japan Tourist Bureau circulars and returns them, as the Department already has them.
subfiles.title: Letter from Erle R. Dickover to Fred L. Haskett Returning Japanese Tourist Circulars

subfiles.about: A thirteen-year-old boy writes to Joseph C. Grew congratulating him on his appointment, praising his book, and inquiring about Japanese history and future relations.
subfiles.summary: Thirteen-year-old Joe Rice of Magnolia, Arkansas, praises Joseph C. Grew and 'Ten Years in Japan' and asks for guidance on Japanese history.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joe Rice to Joseph C. Grew Concerning Relations with Japan

subfiles.about: The Chief of the Division of Japanese Affairs responds on behalf of Joseph C. Grew to provide young Joe Rice with recommended readings on Japanese history.
subfiles.summary: Erle R. Dickover answers Joe Rice for Grew with a reading list on Japanese history, including Sansom, Murdoch and Brinkley.
subfiles.title: Letter from Erle R. Dickover to Joe Rice Providing a Bibliography on Japanese History

subfiles.about: A confidential cross-reference sheet noting a diplomatic report that the Portuguese diplomatic corps is being evacuated from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram No. 4321 (December 30, 1944) reporting removal of the Portuguese diplomatic corps from Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Evacuation of Portuguese Diplomatic Corps from Tokyo
